features.title: Built for your exam
features.body: Tell us your goal — USMLE Step 1 or Step 2 CK, anatomy, pharmacology, or your country's licensing exam — and Flashcard Guru recommends a community Anki deck and tunes your daily pace to the time you have.

features.title: Import from Anki, export anytime
features.body: Drop in any .apkg or .colpkg package — decks, notes, scheduling state, and media all migrate intact, powered by Anki's own engine. Export back out whenever you want; your progress is never trapped.

features.title: Let AI build the cards
features.body: Paste up to 200 terms and AI fills in the definition, IPA, and an example sentence for each. Or highlight a passage in the built-in reader and generate review-ready cards — you stay in control of what gets sent.

features.title: FSRS review, plus Cram Mode
features.body: Every card schedules itself with the FSRS algorithm — tighter intervals when you're shaky, wider when you're solid. The night before an exam, switch to Cram Mode to run a whole deck without touching your schedule.

features.title: Wireless Anki Remote
features.body: Drive Anki Desktop reviews from your iPhone over Wi-Fi. Free companion add-on, and it works with cheap 8BitDo controllers AnkiMobile won't pair with. Set up →

features.title: Private by default
features.body: Your decks, PDFs, and notes live on your device. AI requests only fire when you explicitly start a generation, with full disclosure of what gets sent. Privacy policy

ankiRemote.metaTitle: Flashcard Guru Remote — Free wireless Anki remote for iPhone
ankiRemote.metaDescription: Turn your iPhone into a wireless review remote for Anki Desktop. Free LGPL-3.0 add-on, paired in 10 seconds via QR code, supports cheap 8BitDo controllers AnkiMobile won't pair with.

hero.title: Anki Remote, on the iPhone you already have
hero.lead: Pair your iPhone with Anki Desktop in 10 seconds via QR code, then drive Show Answer / Again / Hard / Good / Easy from your couch, treadmill, or wherever you're studying. Plug in a cheap 8BitDo controller and it works through your phone — even the models AnkiMobile refuses to pair with.

setup.title: Setup (3 steps, ~1 minute)
setup.step1Lead: On your Mac: open Anki, then Tools → Add-ons → Get Add-ons… and paste this code:
setup.step1Tail: Restart Anki when prompted. The first time the add-on starts, macOS asks "Allow incoming connections?" — click Allow.
setup.step2: On your iPhone: install Flashcard Guru from the App Store.
step3Lines: In Anki: Tools → Connect Phone (Flashcard Guru Remote)… — a QR code appears.
In Flashcard Guru: Settings → Anki Remote → Pair with Mac — scan the QR.
setup.step3Tail: That's it. Open any deck on your Mac and your iPhone takes over.

controllers.title: Hardware controller support
controllers.intro: Plug a controller into your iPhone (USB-C or Bluetooth) and Flashcard Guru forwards the buttons to Anki Desktop:
controllers.keyboardHeading: Keyboard mode (8BitDo Zero 2 / micro / external keyboards)
controllers.footnote: The keyboard route is the trick that makes cheap 8BitDo controllers work — those small models don't expose Apple's GCExtendedGamepad profile, so AnkiMobile rejects them. Flashcard Guru listens to GCKeyboard too, which is what 8BitDo's "Keyboard Mode" sends.

privacy.title: Privacy
bullets: LAN only. The pairing token never leaves your local Wi-Fi. The add-on rejects connections from non-private IPs as a safety check.
No telemetry. No analytics, no remote logging, no upload of your decks or cards.
Revocable any time. "Forget" the iPhone in Anki's pairing dialog and the token is invalidated immediately.

items.q: Does this work with AnkiMobile (the official iOS Anki app)?
items.a: No. This is the companion to Flashcard Guru, our standalone iOS flashcard app. The add-on talks WebSocket to Flashcard Guru on your iPhone, not to AnkiMobile.

items.q: Why isn't this just a Bluetooth keyboard like StudyRemote?
items.a: iOS doesn't allow third-party apps to act as Bluetooth HID peripherals — that limitation is platform-level, not something we can work around. The Wi-Fi WebSocket route lets us deliver the same review actions without that restriction.

items.q: Does it work on Windows or Linux?
items.a: Probably yes — the Python add-on is cross-platform — but we only actively QA on macOS. Anki 2.1.55+ on Qt6 builds is the minimum supported version.

items.q: How do I update the add-on?
items.a: Anki Desktop checks for add-on updates automatically. Tools → Add-ons shows the version; Check for Updates pulls newer ones from AnkiWeb.

items.q: Is the iOS app open source?
items.a: The add-on is open source under LGPL-3.0: jyehn/flashcard-guru-remote-addon. The iOS app itself stays closed-source.
